statements.speaker: Mike Rounds
statements.context: Said to AP about Congress's past delegation of tariff authority to the executive branch.
statements.quote: So they've given authorities to the executive branch over a period of years.
statements.test: True if statutes passed by Congress in different years give the executive branch authority to impose or adjust tariffs (for example Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 or the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977). False if no statute delegates tariff authority to the executive. Cannot be determined if the statutory record does not show who holds the authority.
statements.finding: The U.S. Code, read in AskAmerica's law.usc_sections table, gives the President or the U.S. Trade Representative power over imports under statutes enacted in different years: Section 232 (19 U.S.C. 1862, enacted 1962) lets the President act to "adjust the imports" of an article, Section 301 (19 U.S.C. 2411, enacted 1974) assigns actions to the Trade Representative, and the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1702, enacted 1977) lets the President regulate or prohibit importation.

evidence.label: law.usc_sections (19 U.S.C. 1862, 19 U.S.C. 2411, 50 U.S.C. 1702: headings and source credits)
evidence.sql: SELECT title_number, section_number, heading, source_credit, substr(section_text,1,300) AS t FROM law.usc_sections WHERE (title_number=19 AND section_number IN ('1862','2411')) OR (title_number=50 AND section_number='1702')

evidence.label: law.usc_sections (19 U.S.C. 1862(c): action by the President to adjust imports)
evidence.sql: SELECT substr(section_text, position('(c)' IN section_text), 700) AS t FROM law.usc_sections WHERE title_number=19 AND section_number='1862'

statements.speaker: Steve Womack
statements.context: Said to AP about the effect of tariffs on affordability.
statements.quote: have played a role in some of the affordability issues

statements.speaker: Steve Womack
statements.context: Said to AP about producers in his Arkansas district and tariff costs.
statements.quote: I have producers in my district that lament the fact that they're paying higher for goods that can't be sourced domestically
statements.test: True if a public record (testimony, statements, local reporting or trade data) shows producers in Arkansas's 3rd congressional district paying higher prices for tariffed goods that have no domestic source. False if the record shows producers there face no such higher costs. Cannot be determined if no record of those producers' costs or complaints is found.
statements.finding: Statewide reporting by Little Rock Public Radio (July 1, 2025) describes Arkansas growers paying more for fertilizer and equipment under tariffs and an Arkansas importer saying his China-sourced products are no longer made in the United States. No record found names producers in the 3rd district or their costs, so the evidence does not speak to the district-level point; AskAmerica's warehouse has no state- or district-level import data.

evidence.label: Little Rock Public Radio: Arkansas farmers, manufacturers decry new tariff policy (2025-07-01)

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: PBS NewsHour's host stated that the president acknowledged his role in Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive of Nvidia.
statements.quote: Reported as: President Trump acknowledged he personally pushed for it.
statements.test: True if President Trump publicly said he personally pushed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive. False if he publicly denied any role in it. Cannot be determined if no public statement by him on his role is found.
statements.finding: As reported by NBC News and CNBC from his Nov. 23, 2026 phone interview with CNBC, Trump said "I believe my intervention was very important" and that he had spoken to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly" and convinced them. No transcript of the interview or White House page could be read directly; "personally pushed" is the PBS host's wording.

evidence.label: NBC News: Trump says he spoke 'directly and indirectly' with Nvidia's board
CNBC: Trump sealed deal for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang as CEO

statements.speaker: Greg Abbott
statements.context: Said in an archived recording from his summer 2026 campaign about proposed AI data centers in Texas neighborhoods.
statements.quote: Pushing back against these AI data centers that are trying to build in our neighborhoods.

selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 27 or 28, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 28, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus every transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (none was). PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. One listed NPR story (Week in Politics, Nov. 28) returned no readable text and was not used. Transcripts from Nov. 22 to 25 were searched only to confirm quotes; none held any of the day's quotes. Reporters' and commentators' paraphrases of opinions, an AI-generated voice in a campaign ad, and statements by people outside the offices in scope (including a governor-elect and state attorneys general) were left out. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them.
lede: Eleven officeholders in scope were quoted in the day's politics coverage from NPR and PBS NewsHour. Most of the statements came from an Associated Press story on members of Congress reconsidering tariffs after the November election.

Nine members of Congress spoke about tariffs: Republicans Todd Young, Michael Guest, John Kennedy, Mike Rounds, Steve Womack, Josh Hawley and Rand Paul, and Democrats Ron Wyden and Richard Neal. Their statements covered Congress's role in setting tariffs, tariffs on Canada, the effect of tariffs on costs, and whether a repeal bill could become law.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott was heard in an archived campaign recording about AI data centers, and PBS NewsHour reported that President Donald Trump acknowledged pushing for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive. Three statements were checkable: two were supported and one was unsettled.
